newsitem.title: KENYA: Uganda parades captured Sudanese, rebels to reporters.
newsitem.headline: Uganda parades captured Sudanese, rebels to reporters.

text.p: Uganda on Sunday allowed reporters to speak to 114 Sudanese soldiers and 16 Ugandan rebels it said were captured inside its northern border, Radio Uganda said.
The radio, monitored in Nairobi, said Ugandan armed forces believed those captured had fled their bases in Southern Sudan to escape attacks from the Sudan People's Liberation Army (SPLA).
It quoted a Sudanese officer as saying he had been captured on April 9, but was unsure in which country.
The report said the Ugandan rebels -- members of the Lord's Resistance Army (LRA) and including women and children -- looked thin and said they had not eaten for weeks.
Sudan accuses Ugandan troops of fighting alongside the SPLA in the south, while Kampala accuses Khartoum of aiding the LRA.
Uganda on Friday said its army killed 60 Sudanese soldiers and captured more than 100 just inside Uganda, beating back a joint attack by the Sudanese army and Ugandan rebels.
Forces under SPLA leader John Garang's command have this year stepped up their war to topple Khartoum's Islamist government in a rebel coalition called the National Democratic Alliance (NDA).
Since 1983 the SPLA has fought for independence or greater autonomy for the Christian and animist south from the Moslem and Arab north. The NDA says it aims to trigger a popular uprising in Khartoum.
The LRA is a collection of roaming gangs headed by Joseph Kony waging an insurgency in northern Uganda.
